title: Word search
statement: Return whether the word can be traced on the grid through horizontally or vertically adjacent cells, using each cell at most once.
hints: DFS from each cell, marking the path in place and restoring on return.
Prune before searching: letter counts; and search from the rarer end of the word.

solution.explanation: Mark visited cells in place (and restore them: that's the backtrack). The adversarial cases (a grid of A's with a missing letter at the end) defeat plain DFS; two cheap prunings fix them: if the board lacks enough of some letter, answer False immediately; and if the first letter is more common than the last, search the reversed word, so the search fails early.
solution.python:
def exist(board, word):
    R_, C = len(board), len(board[0])
    from collections import Counter
    have = Counter(ch for row in board for ch in row)
    if any(have[c] < k for c, k in Counter(word).items()): return False
    if have[word[0]] > have[word[-1]]: word = word[::-1]
    def dfs(r, c, i):
        if i == len(word): return True
        if not (0 <= r < R_ and 0 <= c < C) or board[r][c] != word[i]: return False
        board[r][c] = "#"
        ok = dfs(r + 1, c, i + 1) or dfs(r - 1, c, i + 1) or dfs(r, c + 1, i + 1) or dfs(r, c - 1, i + 1)
        board[r][c] = word[i]
        return ok
    return any(dfs(r, c, 0) for r in range(R_) for c in range(C))
